PullRequest.Title: automations: fix: enable supported worktree targets
PullRequest.Body:
# Fix falsely disabled automation worktree selection

## Contents

- [Stack and purpose](#stack-and-purpose)
- [Root cause](#root-cause)
- [Included fixes](#included-fixes)
- [Explicit exclusions](#explicit-exclusions)
- [Validation](#validation)

## Stack and purpose

This is the smaller replacement for the worktree portion of [#335018](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335018).

It is based on the revert branch in [#335591](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335591), not directly on main, so this PR's diff contains only the seven worktree/startup fixes. Review and land the revert first, then this PR. The remaining provider configuration changes are held in [draft #335595](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335595), stacked on this branch.

The goal is that **New Worktree is selectable for a supported Codex, Claude, or other Agent Host automation target**, while unavailable or non-repository targets are rejected instead of silently promising isolation.

## Root cause

The automation dialog read a session-type capability that was hard-coded to Copilot CLI. Codex and Claude therefore appeared unsupported even though the Agent Host owns worktree isolation for their sessions.

The dialog also used the local Git extension to discover every target's repository and branches. That cannot discover repositories on a remote Agent Host. Merely removing the Copilot-only flag would leave remote targets incorrectly unavailable.

## Included fixes

1. Advertise host-owned worktree configuration for all advertised Agent Host agents. Workspace-specific support still comes from the host's schema.
2. Obtain workspace support, current branch, and branch choices through a provider-owned operation. Remote search reuses the resolved context, and partial completion results do not falsely mark saved branches unavailable.
3. Allow opting out of a saved Worktree selection when support disappears.
4. After opting out, require normal repository availability before Worktree can be selected again; a retained branch is not a bypass.
5. Validate workspace-specific worktree support when the configure tool creates or changes an explicit worktree target. Unsupported/missing options reject the target, cancellation makes no changes, and provider errors are not silently treated as success. Legacy providers without the optional operation retain their previous behavior.
6. Coalesce duplicate repository lookups from related target/provider notifications.
7. Mark generated session IDs worktree-pending before eager provider startup. This prevents Codex prewarming in the source checkout before host isolation is ready; failed creation cleans the pending state.

The implementation remains provider-neutral in shared Sessions code. Tests cover supported provider choices, remote branch discovery/search, unavailable targets, cancellation and recovery, and startup ordering.

## Explicit exclusions

This PR does **not** change:

- Cloud model restoration, compatibility fields, or Sandbox routing;
- fallback CLI approval-policy preference handling;
- custom-agent first-turn inheritance or Codex custom-agent restoration;
- provider-native configuration toolbars;
- the shared ActionList implementation or its tests.

Those provider-configuration and custom-agent fixes are held for separate draft review. The shared IME fix is independently tracked in [#335578](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335578).

Until that IME fix lands, cancelling composition during a pending remote branch search without changing the query can leave the picker loading. Changing the query or reopening it remains the workaround. This smaller PR does not claim to fix that shared-component edge case.

## Validation

- **977 targeted unit tests passed**, with 27 existing pending tests.
- **Five strict real-provider replay scenarios passed**, covering host branch configuration, Copilot/Claude/Codex working directories, and automation configuration after host restart.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Changed-file ESLint, `git diff --check`, and normal commit hygiene passed.
- The diff is **seven focused commits across 12 files**, with no Cloud provider, custom-agent execution, native configuration-picker, or ActionList files.
- The source changes are reintroduced from the previously reviewed worktree fixes. A Cloud-only regression was moved to the draft remainder rather than pulling its unrelated suite into this PR.
- Full Code OSS, Component Fixtures and CodeQL pull-request workflows target `main`/release branches; they do not run against this stacked feature-branch base. After the revert lands, retarget this PR to main and require the normal CI before landing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening and editing new-session repository/provider configuration, including an Automation draft
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker renders from the provider's already-resolved config; changing a value can trigger the existing agent-host resolveSessionConfig round trip before the updated schema is usable. The diff removes the Automation-dialog menu registration and does not add work to the remaining new-session render path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve provider-owned session configuration and dynamic branch completions through the agent-host connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One config resolution per applicable draft/config update; branch completions are query-driven and cancellation-bounded, not per schema property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider resolution path existed; the changed picker code removes its Automation-menu instance and leaves ordinary new-session rendering at the same O(number of schema properties) cost.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution must complete before updated provider configuration or branch choices are available; rendering itself uses cached resolvedConfig.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of provider schema properties during render and number of explicit configuration/search interactions; no new collection fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Config resolutions use sequence numbers to discard stale responses; completion requests are cancellation-bounded. The diff does not alter this scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rendering reads cached session config. Dynamic completion results are request-scoped; no cache lifecycle is added or removed by the changed lines.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: menu removal and unchanged cached render path are explicit in the diff and surrounding provider code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider schema size and remote-host latency vary, but the diff removes an Automation surface rather than increasing requests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; no new synchronous UI, IPC, or scaling work is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selecting a model for a new Cloud session and later sending the request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A model selection updates observable state, scans the already-loaded model option items for the selected id, and updates the in-memory chat-session option before send. The eventual network/provider send remains the dominant boundary and is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update the in-memory chat-session option map and emit its local change event
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one local option update per explicit Cloud model selection; lookup is O(number of advertised models).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: RemoteNewSession.setModelId previously performed the same model-group lookup and option update on every call; the diff moves it to the provider's explicit model-selection path, reducing rather than increasing invocation scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous local work on the selection path; it does not itself cross IPC or network.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the Cloud chat request through the existing provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider request per user send, independent of model option count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cloud sends already consumed the selected session options; the diff does not add another send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the request critical path, but unchanged by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Advertised model count for the local find and user model-selection frequency; realistic effective cardinality is one lookup/update per explicit selection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model selection is synchronous local state mutation; request concurrency is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Option groups and selected options are held by the existing chat session. The diff removes synchronization on every option-group notification and adds no cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both old and new synchronization sites and the local implementation of setSessionOption are visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Model catalogs vary in size, but expected lists are bounded and the changed placement narrows work frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; work is moved off broad setModelId/notification paths onto explicit Cloud user selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating, prewarming, sending to, or resuming a Codex session with workspace customizations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Codex builds customization launch data before thread/start, first-turn validation, thread/resume, and customization reconciliation. Workspace-agent/skill filesystem discovery and Codex subprocess requests remain on those paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover workspace agents and skills, read selected customization files, and write generated agent-role TOML files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Discovery scales with configured workspace roots and customization entries each time launch state is rebuilt; role-file writes scale with discovered roles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These discovery/read/write operations already existed. The diff removes an additional worktree metadata read and, for linked roots, potential Git repository/worktree resolution from each launch build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On materialization, send validation, resume, and customization reconciliation critical paths; prewarm can perform it off the first-send path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start, resume, unsubscribe, or send a turn to the Codex app-server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one thread start or resume and one turn request per relevant session action; restart is signature-gated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same app-server calls and signature checks existed; the changed customization code does not add calls or concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Thread materialization/resume and turn requests are user-visible critical-path operations; prewarm thread creation is background when allowed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace root count, customization file count, selected agent-role count, and number of session materialize/send/resume events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Agent and skill discovery run in parallel; selected capability stats are parallelized; customization reconciliation is sequenced per session. Prewarm is skipped while worktree resolution is pending.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Materialized customization signatures suppress unnecessary thread restarts, although launch data is rebuilt for comparison. The diff preserves this behavior and removes worktree metadata/Git lookups.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all _buildCustomizationLaunch callers and boundaries are explicit, and deleted code contains the removed metadata/Git operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and Git latency vary by workspace, but the changed code clearly reduces boundary work rather than adding it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; this path has less boundary work after the diff. There is insufficient evidence of a shipped performance symptom to record it as a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting a durable Automation run and forwarding its first message
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The service persists run state, creates one provider session, links it, then starts that session with one message. The changed code conditionally clones the message only when it must inject a session model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and start the provider-backed automation session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create and one start per accepted run; active runs are deduplicated before this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same create/start calls occurred. Previously the message was always object-spread; now it is reused unless a model must be injected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both operations are on the automation startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct the first-turn message passed to the execution service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shallow clone per run only when the message lacks a model and the session supplies one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every run shallow-cloned the message and could add model/agent fields; the diff reduces allocation frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Negligible local work before the existing session start boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Automation run frequency and message property count; no per-history-item or unbounded collection work is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Duplicate active runs are coalesced by the existing active-run check; state mutations remain serialized through the existing mutation queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or retained collection is introduced; durable run maps follow existing lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the before/after allocation and unchanged session boundaries are explicit in the hunk.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Message objects may vary in size, but the changed allocation is strictly no greater than before.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the change reduces shallow-copy work and leaves boundary cardinality unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating and maintaining Copilot CLI session permission state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Permission state is initialized at session creation and read when capturing/sending configuration. The diff removes a per-session configuration-change observable/listener and computes policy clamping only when choosing the default.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and lifetime of open new sessions and configuration-change event frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable updates only; no queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The per-session derived observable and event subscription are removed, reducing retained listener state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener creation and derived observable removal are directly shown in the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical open-session counts are modest, but the direction of change is a reduction in retained objects and event work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; lifecycle and event costs decrease.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and their relevant callers. The diff primarily removes menu instances, listeners, repeated option synchronization, and worktree metadata/Git resolution; remaining boundary cardinality and critical paths are unchanged. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
